source_spans.locator: Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.114-115, abstract: two post-learning physiological phases support different stabilization processes
Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published pp.118-119, systems-level redistribution and local strengthening sections
Nature Reviews Neuroscience 11, published p.123, Figure 3 and conclusion: sequential contributions of the two phases

conditions: post-learning physiological state with an earlier synchronized phase followed by a later desynchronized phase
temporal_scope: newly acquired representations are processed across sequential post-learning phases and across systems-level and local timescales

nodes.description: newly acquired representation initially supported by a fast temporary store and related cortical sites
earlier post-learning phase characterized by widespread synchronized activity and repeated reactivation
reactivation-driven redistribution and integration of newly acquired representations into distributed cortical networks
later post-learning phase characterized by more locally encapsulated activity
local strengthening and stabilization of connections supporting representations processed in the prior phase
ordered separation between the earlier systems-level phase and later local-strengthening phase

relations.description: the earlier synchronized phase normally precedes the later desynchronized phase in the proposed sequence
reactivation during the earlier phase promotes redistribution and integration of the newly acquired representation across systems
later local strengthening is proposed to occur preferentially in the later phase and to stabilize representations reorganized earlier
the source assigns different processing roles and timescales to the two ordered phases rather than treating post-learning change as one undifferentiated process
